title: Checking GMO claims and leading fair conversations
course_title: Genetically Modified Organisms and Modern Biotechnology

say: Checking GMO claims, and leading fair conversations.
This is the video for module three of Genetically Modified Organisms and Modern Biotechnology.
This module turns your knowledge into community leadership. The aim is not to win arguments. It is to reach a fair verdict you can explain.

panel.heading: From knowledge to leadership
items: Test any claim with one method

say: You will learn a scoring method for any claim, a plan for a balanced community conversation, and the final project that brings it together.

panel.heading: From knowledge to leadership
items: Test any claim with one method

say: First, rewrite the claim as one clear sentence. Vague claims like GMOs are poison name no crop or effect.

panel.heading: Five questions, scored 0 to 2
items: Is it about here and now?

say: Second, the type: food safety, environment, economics or law. Does the evidence match? A seed price cannot prove a health danger.

panel.heading: Five questions, scored 0 to 2
items: Is it about here and now?

say: Third, the source. A regulator, WHO or a named study scores 2. An anonymous forward scores 0.

panel.heading: Five questions, scored 0 to 2
items: Is it about here and now?

say: Fourth, can you follow the evidence to the original document? And fifth, is it about an approved product in your country, and current? Add the scores for a total out of 10.

panel.heading: Five questions, scored 0 to 2
items: Is it about here and now?

say: For example, Chioma, a nurse in Port Harcourt, scores two messages from her church group. The first names no crop, no evidence and an unnamed doctor. It scores 1 out of 10.

panel.heading: Chioma scores two WhatsApp claims
items: Claim 1: GM foods cause cancer, a doctor said so
Claim 2: GM cowpea will end hunger in Nigeria

say: The second is in favour of GMOs. It came from a seed advert with no yield or price data. It scores 3. Hunger also depends on prices, storage, income and conflict.

panel.heading: Chioma scores two WhatsApp claims
items: Claim 1: GM foods cause cancer, a doctor said so
Claim 2: GM cowpea will end hunger in Nigeria

say: Both score 3 or less, so she forwards neither. She posts one calm message with WHO's statement and a link to NBMA's website. Score a claim you like with the same care as one you dislike.

panel.heading: Chioma scores two WhatsApp claims
items: Claim 1: GM foods cause cancer, a doctor said so
Claim 2: GM cowpea will end hunger in Nigeria
panel.rule: 8 to 10 credible. 4 to 7 check more. 0 to 3 do not repeat it.

say: Watch for absolute words, fear language and no checkable source.

panel.heading: Warning signs on both sides
right: GMOs have no risks at all

say: The same signs appear on the other side: no risks at all, miracle language, and studies nobody can find.

panel.heading: Warning signs on both sides
right: GMOs have no risks at all

say: Scammers use these fears and hopes. Be careful with anyone selling a test kit to detect GMO in your food.

panel.heading: Scams use GMO fears and hopes

cards.d: Be careful with anyone selling a kit to detect GMO in your food at home.
A remedy to remove GMO from your body is a warning sign. Do not send money.
Unlabelled seed sold as a new GM variety outside a registered dealer. Ask NBMA first.

say: Or a remedy to remove GMO from your body.

panel.heading: Scams use GMO fears and hopes

cards.d: Be careful with anyone selling a kit to detect GMO in your food at home.
A remedy to remove GMO from your body is a warning sign. Do not send money.
Unlabelled seed sold as a new GM variety outside a registered dealer. Ask NBMA first.

say: Or seed claiming to be an approved GM variety outside a registered dealer. Do not send money or personal details. Ask NBMA or your extension office first.

say: Facts alone rarely change minds. People care about their children's health, their money and their land. For example, Grace leads a 25-member cooperative in Plateau. She welcomes people, then writes what they have heard on a flip chart.

panel.heading: Grace's 30-minute session
items: Sort concerns into four types: 5 minutes

say: Together they sort concerns into the four types. Many arguments disappear once people see they are different questions.

panel.heading: Grace's 30-minute session
items: Sort concerns into four types: 5 minutes

say: She reads WHO's sentence aloud exactly as written, and shows NBMA's website. Then farmers speak first on open questions like seed cost and refuge rules.

panel.heading: Grace's 30-minute session
items: Sort concerns into four types: 5 minutes

say: It adds up to 30 minutes, with 21 for the group to talk and only 6 for facts. If you do not know an answer, say, I do not know yet, I will ask and report back.

panel.heading: Grace's 30-minute session
items: Sort concerns into four types: 5 minutes
panel.rule: Listen first. Give the group more time than you take.

say: Your project has three parts. Part A: your country's law and regulator, with dates. Mark anything you could not confirm as not confirmed.

cards.d: Your law and regulator, confirmed notices with dates, and how the public can take part.
One real claim, word for word, with five scores and a three-part verdict.
Audience, one message, channel, date, and a number you can count.

say: Part B: one real claim, scored, with a verdict that says what the claim says, what the evidence shows, and what is still uncertain.

cards.d: Your law and regulator, confirmed notices with dates, and how the public can take part.
One real claim, word for word, with five scores and a three-part verdict.
Audience, one message, channel, date, and a number you can count.

say: Part C: an outreach plan. For example, Aisha in Kaduna held a session where 32 of 40 members came, which is 80 percent.

say: To remember. Score claims with five questions, and do not repeat a low score. Watch for warning signs on both sides. Listen before you explain. And recheck the regulator's website, because approvals change.

panel.heading: Remember
items: What, type, source, evidence, here and now
0 to 3 means do not repeat it
Warning signs appear on both sides
Listen first, sort, then share checked facts
Recheck the regulator, because approvals change

say: Your tasks: score three claims from your log, plan a timed session for a group you belong to, and start Parts A, B and C of your project.
